item.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
item.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. item.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
item.description: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The six-week exercise will give players and support staff who were part of the tour an opportunity to share their experiences, although individual accounts will remain confidential and will not be made available to the CA Board. The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations. The document will not include individual testimonies or any supporting material. CA has also committed to releasing the complete report, together with its response, within 30 days of receiving it. The independent exercise will be overseen by senior counsel Fiona McLeod AO SC, who will conduct private sessions with those willing to participate. The forum was announced following fresh revelations surrounding the 2018 scandal in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr . In the book, Khawaja claimed that awareness of the sandpaper plan extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned by CA. David Warner and Cameron Bancroft have supported parts of his account, while Pat Cummins and several other bowlers have maintained that they had no knowledge of the plan. The forum will examine Australia's ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season, the team's involvement in all four Tests of the South Africa tour, and the incident involving Bancroft during the third Test in Cape Town on March 24, 2018. It will also look into CA's subsequent investigation into the episode. However, the exercise is not intended to reopen the original investigation or establish individual responsibility for the incident. CA has extended invitations to all players and support staff who were part of the South Africa tour, along with the management officials and board directors who were associated with the organisation at the time. Participants will be able to share their accounts through face-to-face or online meetings with McLeod, submit written statements or provide relevant documents. Taking part in the process is voluntary, and those who choose to participate will be permitted to have a support person or legal representative present. The terms of reference also lay down safeguards to protect the confidentiality of participants. Information shared by one individual cannot be attributed to them when seeking clarification from another participant unless they provide consent. Those involved will be informed about who can access their submissions and will have the opportunity to verify their own accounts for accuracy. In addition, the forum will be given access to the 2018 Culture and Governance Review of Australian Cricket conducted by The Ethics Centre, along with other relevant records and documents it considers necessary. item.title: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.”
item.description: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.” The strength of Hoffenheim’s bench proved decisive in Thursday evening’s 3-1 Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz. Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club. Hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him. “No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.” Hoffenheim’s substitutes deliver decisive contributions Ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker. Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench. “Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.” Hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen , Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist. Despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half. Baumann acknowledged that Hoffenheim remain in a developmental phase. The German international nevertheless welcomed the response after halftime, which helped lift Ilzer’s side to 15th place in the Europa League standings. Thursday

item.title: Syrian referee refutes ‘drunk’ accusations as ‘insult and defamation’
item.description: A referee has hit back at claims he was “drunk” while officiating an AFC Champions League Two match. Footage has been widely shared on social media of Syrian referee Hanna Hattab looking visibly disoriented during a match between Iran 's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates . One particular incident raised eyebrows when Hattab showed a yellow card to Al Jazira’s goalkeeper for a foul that happened close to the halfway line, 40 yards away from him. Hattab was then replaced at half-time with the fourth official taking over for the remainder of the game, which Al Jazira won 1-0. Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following erratic decision-making as similar accusations flooded in online. But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has refuted the allegations as “insult and defamation”, threatening legal action. He wrote in a statement on Facebook: “I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands. Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them. “I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.” He also said he would issue a further statement following contact with the Syrian Arab Football Federation (SFA) which will “clarify all the details and facts related to what happened ... with full transparency and clarity.” Omani journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian football, has since claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus". The SFA have also put out a statement standing in support of Hattab, while stating it has requested his medical report from the match. “The Main Referees Committee of the Syrian Arab Football Federation confirms that it stands in full support of international referee Mr Hana Khattab regarding the incident he was subjected to, following reassurance about his health,” it said. “This comes after the committee was reassured of his well-being, following a number of discussions on social media concerning the incident. The committee emphasises its full support for him and its commitment to following up on the matter in all its details and developments. “In this regard, the committee has requested that the Syrian Football Referees Committee provide the medical report relating to the referee, the match observers' report and the referee assessor's report. This is in order to establish the circumstances of the incident accurately and comprehensively and to complete the necessary procedures in this matter. “The committee also confirms that it will provide the relevant authorities and the public with the findings as soon as the requested reports are

item.title: Shaquille O’Neal thinks Anthony Edwards can ruin Timberwolves if he fails to notice one thing
item.description: Credit: Marcin Golba/NurPhoto/David Berding via Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves have been doing quite well even without Anthony Edwards, and Shaquille O’Neal has sent the superstar a warning about his eventual return. Anthony Edwards has been out indefinitely since he had arthroscopic surgery on his right knee late in October. The Minnesota Timberwolves superstar has missed the entirety of November, and will likely miss all of December and a fair amount of time in January as well. The Timberwolves haven’t struggled all that much in his absence, either. LaMelo Ball has fit the team like a glove, and they have a 14-5 record going into Friday’s game against the Memphis Grizzlies. With that in mind, Shaquille O’Neal recently shared some advice for the young superstar for when he does return. Shaquille O’Neal says Anthony Edwards will have to ensure he doesn’t disrupt team rhythm after returning The Timberwolves have played excellent team ball in Edwards’ absence. He was averaging over 33 points per game in his four games this season. Since he’s been out, though, the team has five players averaging between 12 points to 19 points per game. No one star has been dominating, and this style has been working quite well. So Shaq thinks Edwards will have to be careful with that when he does come back. “I think it’s going to be up to Anthony Edwards,” O’Neal said. “Because right now, he has to see how the guys are playing. Because they’re only playing like this because they’re eating. See, a lot of time when he has the ball, they’re just sitting in the corner, and they’re really out of rhythm. “Now that he’s not there, LaMelo’s kicking it to a damn rhythm. So he has to see this. So when he gets back, he’s going to have to get his and keep his guys in rhythm.” The likes of Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu, and Jonathan Kuminga are beginning to truly establish themselves within the context of the team. If Edwards can come back and figure out a seamless fit, no team will want to face off against the Timberwolves in the playoffs this season. item.title: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling
item.description: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling Joshua Kimmich made headlines earlier this week after publicly criticising the Bayern Munich hierarchy over their comments on Jamal Musiala's neurological condition and the possibility of adjusting his salary. His comments subsequently sparked speculation over whether he could face disciplinary action, potentially in the form of a fine. However, Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund has now made it clear that no such punishment is being considered. “We never discussed that, and imposing a fine was never a topic of conversation. We're really looking forward and focusing on the upcoming games,” Freund said at Friday's press conference. Sitting alongside Freund, head coach Vincent Kompany was also asked about the vice-captain's outspoken comments but declined to elaborate. Instead, he emphasised that internal matters should remain behind closed doors. “I understand what this question is getting at. However, I can't help you any further with these matters at the moment. We have our bubble, and that's how it will stay," Kompany said. “That doesn't mean we simply applaud everything internally. We tell each other the truth and openly address what hasn't gone well. But I protect these matters, and I lead by example in that regard. “If I were to comment on other issues now, I wouldn't be living up to that standard. My priority is the game against Hamburg.”

item.title: Barcelona injury crisis raises alarm across men’s and women’s teams and Barça Atlètic
item.description: Barcelona injury crisis raises alarm across men’s and women’s teams and Barça Atlètic Barcelona are facing growing concern over an injury crisis affecting several sections of the club, with the men’s and women’s first teams, Barça Atlètic and even the basketball side all struggling with player absences, according to a report from SPORT . The mounting problems have intensified fears that an increasingly congested calendar is taking a physical toll on the club’s athletes across all the divisions. Despite investment in medical staff, rehabilitation support and injury prevention, Barcelona have yet to find a solution to the growing number of setbacks. The situation is particularly troubling for the football department, where Hansi Flick’s first team has repeatedly been forced to manage injuries during demanding stretches of the season. Unfortunately, however, the concern is not limited to the senior squad, with the reserve team also experiencing a difficult run. A packed calendar is testing Barcelona’s prevention work Hansi Flick strengthened the first-team physical preparation staff in July by bringing in Benjamin Kugel , aiming to improve conditioning and reduce late-season injury problems. Hansi Flick has been dealing with player shortages, especially in defence, this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Yet muscle injuries remain a recurring issue amid international travel and matches every three or four days. Specifically, the stretch involving Betis, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid illustrated the cost. Eric García, Jules Kounde, Xavi Espart and Dani Olmo suffered injuries during that period, while Gerard Martin also experienced discomfort . The sequence left Flick managing absences during a demanding run of fixtures. Barça Atlètic faces the most severe shortage The reserve team has been hit especially hard. Before facing Girona B, Juliano Belletti was dealing with a shortage caused by injuries and international call-ups, with reports counting more than 20 unavailable players. Barcelona requested that the fixture be postponed, but it went ahead. Barcelona have suffered several injuries this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The match brought further damage, as Dani Avila and Ibrahim Diarra were injured , while other players finished with physical problems. Barça Atlètic subsequently lost Mirza Catovic in the derby against Espanyol B. Barcelona confirmed that Catovic had suffered a fibula fracture and would be out for around four months, taking the reserve side’s injury list to 12. Unfortunately, Barcelona’s women’s side is also dealing with a difficult injury situation, while the basketball team has been managing absences during a packed domestic and EuroLeague schedule. The pattern across several departments makes the issue bigger than an isolated run of bad luck. Barcelona have invested in prevention and recovery, but workload, travel and limited rest continue to challenge those measures.

item.title: How Milan winger Moreira infuriated Olympiacos fans and players after Europa League goal
item.description: How Milan winger Moreira infuriated Olympiacos fans and players after Europa League goal Milan winger Diego Moreira infuriated Olympiacos fans and players with his goal celebration in a Europa League game in Athens, prompting Rossoneri coach Ruben Amorim to apologise at full time. The incident happened in the final minutes of the game, after the Belgian winger scored to make it 4-2 for the Rossoneri. PIRAEUS, GREECE – NOVEMBER 26: Gelson Martins of Olympiacos FC is put under pressure from Diego Moreira of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Olympiacos FC and AC Milan at Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis on November 26, 2026 in Piraeus, Greece. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) La Gazzetta dello Sport describes what Moreira did to irritate the home fans and players. The Belgian scored in front of the Greek supporters’ stand and stared at it, motionless, for a few seconds. Safe to say that neither the home fans nor their players enjoyed the celebration, as Manolis Saliakas and João Silva confronted the Milan winger. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Diego Moreira of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Silva wagged his finger at him, as to say: ‘You don’t do that in our house.’ A few seconds of tension followed. With Saliakas, there was a grim face-to-face that lasted a few seconds. “It won’t happen again. Moreira is a young lad who plays, but he has to grow,” Milan coach Amorim said at full time. ITALY – NOVEMBER 8: Ruben Amorim, head coach of Milan, looks on prior to kick-off in the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and AC Milan at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on November 8, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) “We know we wouldn’t like it if they did that to our fans. It’s my responsibility, and I apologise, but he didn’t do it with bad intent.” Moreira has now scored five goals in 12 appearances across all competitions with Milan.

item.title: Conflicts, El Nino Worsening Hunger — UN Food Agencies
item.description: UN food agencies warned Friday of worsening hunger over the next six months in 16 mostly African areas, with ongoing conflicts exacerbating already dire conditions in countries like Sudan and Yemen. While armed conflict and violence are the main reasons for acute food insecurity around the globe, dramatic climate events, including El Nino, are another driver, the joint report from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP) said. The Rome-based agencies listed Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen as the areas of highest concern in its early warning about 16 “hunger hotspots” from December until May 2027. Famine remains a “plausible” risk in parts of Sudan — including North Darfur — and South Sudan, the report found. ‘Alarming levels of displacement’ The indoor cooking setup of a local food vendor, featuring large metal pots resting on industrial gas stoves. The stoves are connected directly to an orange gas cylinder running on the clean, smoke-free biogas produced by the biodigester. (Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV) The risk of worsening hunger comes amid a rise in “political violence events” around the world, up by more than 15 percent over the same period a year earlier, which has prompted “alarming levels of displacement in recent months”, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen. In the five countries most at risk, all repeatedly cited on the hotspot list since 2022, humanitarian assistance has declined by nearly two-thirds over the 2022-2025 period, from $5.1 billion to $2 billion. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” wrote FAO and WFP. While past humanitarian assistance helped avert famine, “the gains proved fragile and of limited duration: severe acute food insecurity risks — including risk of famine — re-emerged within a few years.” Also classified as a “very high concern” are Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo — which is also struggling to contend with an outbreak of Ebola — Palestine, and Haiti, where expanding gang violence has displaced 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access. New additions to the list are Chad, Uganda, the Southern Africa region and the Central American Dry Corridor, a tropical dry forest extending from Guatemala to Costa Rica, with the latter two regions expected to be hit by the effects of El Nino, adversely affecting crops. The list also includes Mali, Myanmar and Madagascar. “Targeted humanitarian action is urgently needed to save lives and livelihoods across all hunger hotspots,” read the report. “In hotspots of highest concern, such action is critical to prevent starvation and loss of life.” Too much or little rain El Nino — the ocean warming phenomenon that is disrupting weather patterns globally, provoking devastating droughts or in

item.title: Fabio Cannavaro reveals Liverpool star Virgil van Dijk's desire to play in Serie A amid AC Milan links
item.description: 버질 판데이크 (Virgil van Dijk) - Getty Images Fabio Cannavaro has revealed that Liverpool centre-back Virgil van Dijk expressed a desire to play in Serie A during a conversation at the World Cup. With the Dutchman's contract expiring in June 2027, the Italy legend believes a switch to AC Milan would be an exciting move. Van Dijk eyes Italian football adventure Liverpool could face a battle to keep hold of Van Dijk as speculation grows over his long-term future . The Dutch centre-back has reportedly emerged on Milan's radar ahead of next season. Former Italy international Cannavaro has now added fuel to those rumours in an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport . The 2006 Ballon d'Or winner disclosed that Van Dijk is genuinely intrigued by the prospect of testing himself in Italian football. Van Dijk existing deal with Liverpool is set to expire in June 2027, leaving the door open for potential suitors to monitor his availability. Cannavaro backs Dutchman for Milan switch Cannavaro explained that his insight came directly from a personal conversation with the Liverpool defender during the World Cup. Having represented Napoli, Parma, Juventus, and Inter during his own career, the Italian icon believes Milan would be a fitting destination. "I saw him at the World Cup and he told me that he would like to have an experience in Italy," Cannavaro said. "He is very fascinated by it. It would be nice to see Van Dijk at Milan." Physical dominance and the Maldini comparison While Cannavaro is clearly an admirer of Van Dijk's attributes, he also offered a candid tactical assessment of how elite defenders evolve over time. Drawing on his own experiences and an anecdote involving Paolo Maldini, Cannavaro highlighted the vital role of pace in defending. "In recent years, he has combined great physical strength with outstanding speed," Cannavaro noted. "Once, a coach said to Paolo Maldini: 'You turn badly.' And he replied: 'Mister, as long as I get to the ball.'" Cannavaro warned that relying on recovery speed comes with an inevitable caveat later in a player's career. "It was the same for me," he added. "When you are very fast, you can afford a technical error. The problem comes when that speed is no longer there." What next for Van Dijk's future? With Van Dijk's Liverpool contract running until June 2027, the club still hold a strong position regarding his immediate future. However, Milan's reported interest for next season means the Italian side could soon test Liverpool's resolve. Whether Van Dijk decides to act on his fascination with Serie A remains to be seen.

item.title: Botman banned from driving for using phone at wheel
item.description: Newcastle United defender Sven Botman has been banned from driving [PA] Premier League footballer Sven Botman has been banned from driving after being caught using his mobile phone at the wheel. The Newcastle United centre-back pleaded guilty to using a handheld mobile phone while using a motor vehicle on a road at Newcastle Magistrates' Court on Wednesday. The 26-year-old was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months, as these were added to points he had already accrued. He was fined £900 and ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 victim surcharge, the MoJ said. Botman was driving a Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road, in Newcastle, on 17 September when he was spotted using his phone. The Dutchman changed his plea from not guilty to guilty at his court appearance on Wednesday, the MoJ confirmed. Newcastle United signed Botman from Lille in 2022. He has made nine appearances so far this season, scoring one goal. Follow BBC Newcastle on X , Facebook , Nextdoor and Instagram and listen to Radio Newcastle on BBC Sounds .

item.title: Clashes mar European games as Macron condemns violence
item.description: Fan violence marred the tie at the Stade Velodrome [Getty Images] Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia. There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok. In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters. With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions. "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," said the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished". According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media. "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added. "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety." Fan violence mars Marseille-Levski Sofia match Police response to Besiktas fans' pro-Palestine banner 'unacceptable' Sunderland held by Polish side Jagiellonia Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break in a match Marseille won 1-0. "It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski Sofia coach Julio Velazquez Marseille boss Bruno Genesio added: "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable." item.title: 'Massive for both' - Saints and Boro revisit Spygate rivalry
item.description: "I don't want to shut out the noise, we just need to know that it's coming and it's going to be electric." The "noise" Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert refers to has been building over recent weeks, with 'Spygate' returning to the collective consciousness as Saints and Middlesbrough meet on Friday (20:00 GMT) for the first time since the scandal. The most recent time they came face-to-face was in last season's Championship play-off semi-finals. Saints ended up winning over the two legs, but were then expelled from the final having being caught spying on a Boro training session before the first match at the Riverside. It turned into a five-month saga which started with a Saints performance analyst being photographed from behind a tree, and ended with Eckert being handed a suspended ban and fined £28,000. The German head coach signed a new deal at Saints exactly a week ago and previously admitted the experience of Spygate had changed his life. Now St Mary's awaits as the two sides will re-ignite their rivalry after a tough end to the last campaign for both. Saints players felt aggrieved for not being allowed to feature in the play-off final, while Boro suffered the heartbreak of losing at Wembley, as Hull City won promotion to the Premier League. "It's a massive game for both teams," former Nottingham Forest and Ipswich defender Luke Chambers told the 72+ podcast. "Middlesbrough have bounced back tremendously well from the play-offs, the ups and downs, they didn't know if they were coming or going, and to go through that heartache of making the final and not getting over the line - credit to them. "It will be an electric atmosphere and there will be added needle on the pitch, especially with some of the things that happened in the games between the two sides last season when the news broke out." Hellberg reveals Eckert apology after Spygate Southampton give head coach Eckert new deal 'It's changed my life' - Eckert on Spygate scandal Hellberg and Eckert ready to move on - but can supporters? Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg had to be seperated during last season's play-off semi-final [Getty Images] Boro boss Kim Hellberg and Eckert both arrived at their respective clubs in November 2025 and have enjoyed plenty of success on the pitch over the past 12 months. But following the 2-1 defeat in May's play-off semi-final second leg at St Mary's, Hellberg described it as "one of the toughest days" in his coaching career. Although Friday's game promises to be filled with emotion on the pitch and in the stands, the two head coaches claim to have made up since the events of last season after Eckert called Hellberg to apologise over the summer. "We spoke and he called me. I've always been a person who wants to give people a second chance," Hellberg told BBC Radio Tees. item.title: 2027: Lokpobiri rallies Bayelsa West for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, has urged voters in Bayelsa West Senatorial District to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. Lokpobiri made the appeal on Thursday, November 26, during a pre-campaign sensitisation exercise organised by the Bayelsa West APC Campaign Directorate in Aleibiri, Ebedebiri and Agbere communities. Addressing party members, stakeholders and residents, the minister urged them to remain committed to the APC, saying sustained support for the party was necessary to consolidate the reforms and transformation being pursued by the Tinubu administration under its Renewed Hope Agenda. He said Tinubu had demonstrated the courage, vision and determination to reposition the country through what he described as bold reforms and purposeful leadership. “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has remained committed to delivering on his Renewed Hope mandate and transforming our dear nation. The progress being made requires our collective support and commitment to ensure that the gains are sustained. We must therefore give him another mandate in 2027,” he said. The minister also called on the people to support all APC candidates, stressing that political unity, grassroots mobilisation and collective participation would be crucial to the party’s prospects in the elections. “I urge the good people of Bayelsa West to stand firmly with President Tinubu and all APC candidates. This is the time to consolidate our structures, strengthen our grassroots engagement and work together towards victory,” he added. The sensitisation exercise, according to the organisers, was part of the party’s efforts to strengthen grassroots mobilisation, encourage peaceful political participation and build support structures across Bayelsa West ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Lucas Herbert claims he's 'owed a lot' of money from LIV Golf as he suggests whether he regrets joining the league
item.description: Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images LIV Golf officially applied for bankruptcy and began the process of going into liquidation earlier this month. Their plans for a new version of the league – LIV 2.0 – failed to get off the ground after they failed to get enough players to sign up to the project. After many years of bullish promises, LIV Golf is finally finished and the fallout from their collapse will be ongoing for quite some time. LIV Golf may have made a lot of big-name players incredibly wealthy initially, but a lot of golfers have been left in the lurch over the past 12 months regarding payments they’re due. However, it is tough to extract money from a business that has entered into bankruptcy. One golfer in particular is claiming that he is owed a lot of money from the former Saudi-backed league. Lucas Herbert claims he’s ‘owed a lot’ of money from LIV Golf The talented Lucas Herbert spoke with Fox Sports Australia about his recent exit from LIV Golf. The 30-year-old Australian claimed he’s still owed a lot of money from LIV, but suggested that he doesn’t regret his decision to join the league in the first place. “ You’re probably foolish to think you’re going to get much of it. Anything from this point is going to be a bonus, “ Herbert said. “ It’s a long drawn out process with mostly lawyers winning out of the whole battle. I’ve accepted that and moved on. The reality is I made a lot of money at the same time as I’m owed a lot. “ As great as a time I had on the LIV tour, I had many legal issues along the way, which drew a lot of energy out of me. I’ve played this game a few times now and I’m going to expect not very much and hopefully be pleasantly surprised, rather than the other way around. “ I’ve got no problem saying we were poorly communicated with as players throughout the season,” he said. “ A lot of times mainstream media, or media outlets outside of LIV, knew more about what was going on than we did, which was pretty tough to deal with. It was a bit of a contributing factor as to why very few guys were interested in going around again in 2.0. “ It was a tough off-season to have everyone having an opinion on what your livelihood and career and future looks like when you don’t have control over (it) yourself. It’s one thing for people to have their opinions on your poor play, but it felt people at times took pride in seeing everything we tried to build at LIV fail. “ I’m still very happy with the decision I made – it doesn’t look like I’m in a great position right now, but time will tell. “ Herbert is a sensational golfer, so he will undoubtedly make millions of dollars in the future. However, the fact that he is owed so much money from LIV Golf must really be eating away at him. No wonder none of the big names were keen to sign up to LIV 2.0 after being treated so poorly.

item.title: Flyers Game 28: Lines, Notes, & How to Watch vs. Canucks
item.description: The Philadelphia Flyers (9-12-6) will look to get back on track on Friday when they host the Vancouver Canucks (6-20-1) at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Puck drop is at 3:00 PM ET. The Flyers come into Friday’s game after a gut-wrenching 7-3 loss against the Washington Capitals on Wednesday. After a 3-game win streak, the Flyers had a chance to stretch it to 4, but could not get over the hump. They are 3-2-0 over the last 5 games and 5-3-2 over the last 10. The Canucks season has not gotten much better than the last time the Flyers saw them, which wasn’t too long ago. Since the Flyers last saw the Canucks 7 games ago, the Canucks have added 3 more wins, including a 2-3-0 record over the last 5 games and a 3-7-0 record over the last 10. Vancouver has lost its last 2 games. Puck drop is at 3:00 PM ET on Friday. Here is everything you need to know before the game. It’s the beginning of a back-to-back for Philly, but the Flyers will likely want to give Woll a chance to reset before getting him back out there. So, expect Dan Vladar on Friday. Without a morning skate, it’ll be hard to tell exactly what the Flyers will do with their line pairings. Towards the end of the game, head coach Rick Tocchet flipped Cole Knuble and Trevor Zegras , putting Zegras on the 3rd line with Matvei Michkov and Noah Cates. If that sticks, we could get a full game of Michkov and Zegras together. Speaking of Cole Knuble, his garbage-time goal against the Capitals brought him to 5 goals in 14 games this season, which ties him with Denver Barkey (23GP), Tyson Foerster (26GP), Trevor Zegras (27GP), and Christian Dvorak (27GP) for 2nd on the team. It’s a pretty impressive mark for the youngster. Look for him to continue providing a spark for the Flyers on Friday. The Canucks will be without their 2nd highest point-getter, Elias Pettersson (the center), on Friday, as he returned to Vancouver due to injury. As if the Canucks were already struggling enough, it’ll get even harder for them without one of their top offensive threats. item.title: Ex-Man United ace Alejandro Garnacho left staring into the abyss after Aston Villa decision
item.description: Ex-Man United ace Alejandro Garnacho left staring into the abyss after Aston Villa decision Former Manchester United forward Alejandro Garnacho has plunged to a new all-time low, with Aston Villa making a major decision on his future ahead of the January transfer window. Troubles Garnacho was nowhere to be seen on Tuesday evening as Villa suffered a 1-0 Champions League defeat to Galatasaray. Villa boss Unai Emery opted to name 11 substitutes instead of the allowed 12. Emery took the decision amid deepening concerns over the trajectory of Garnacho ‘s career. Since his £40m move from United to Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he has endured a torrid time, having departed after falling out with then-manager Ruben Amorim. He struggled both for form and consistency at Chelsea, managing just one Premier League goal all term. Chelsea decided they had seen enough and approved a move to Villa , initially on loan, with the deal set to become an obligation depending on appearances. But Garnacho has so far failed to impress Emery, both during games and on the training pitch. The Argentine has been omitted from the previous two Premier League squads and has accumulated only 34 minutes of top-flight football. He has made just seven appearances from the bench. According to The Athletic , Villa are actively working to offload the Carrington academy graduate in January. New low The Athletic reports, “Two Villa sources stated in October that they would be amazed if Garnacho did not end up their player beyond the season, with staff being briefed that the initial loan came with the extreme likelihood that Garnacho would transition into a permanent acquisition.” Alejandro Garnacho 2026/27 record Aston Villa · 2026/27 “Garnacho had wanted to leave England before meeting with Emery, who convinced him to stay. But Garnacho has failed to make an impact in Villa’s first-team environment, with performances in training not doing enough to suggest he deserves a chance to play regularly.” “Multiple sources have said Villa are open to his departure in January, provided clubs from overseas come to the table and strike an agreement with his parent club, Chelsea.” It’s understood to be unknown whether Chelsea would want Garnacho, having already considered his exit sealed. Garnacho made 144 appearances for United.

item.title: Pundit says Arsenal players will be uncomfortable if one teammate starts against Man City
item.description: Pundit says Arsenal players will be uncomfortable if one teammate starts against Man City Arsenal could face a significant challenge against Manchester City this weekend if David Raya is unavailable, with Kepa Arrizabalaga potentially continuing in goal. However, former footballer and pundit Paul Dickov believes the Gunners’ defenders may not feel as confident with the Spaniard’s replacement behind them. Raya has established himself as Arsenal’s first choice goalkeeper for much of his time at the Emirates Stadium. His consistency and ability to remain fit have allowed the club to benefit from his performances over the years, making him an important part of their defensive structure. The Spaniard has developed into a world-class goalkeeper and has been among the best in his position over the last few seasons. His contribution has also played an important role in Arsenal’s recent success , particularly through his ability to produce crucial saves when the team has needed him most. Raya’s importance to Arsenal’s defence Without some of the magnificent saves Raya has produced during his time with the Gunners, Arsenal would arguably have struggled to secure several of the victories they have enjoyed. His performances have helped provide the defensive stability that has become a defining feature of their playing style. Arsenal have some of the best defenders in the world, and their approach is built around being organised and difficult to break down. However, the goalkeeper remains an equally important part of that structure, offering security and confidence to those playing in front of him. Raya’s potential absence against Manchester City could therefore create an additional challenge for Mikel Arteta’s side, particularly given the importance of the fixture. (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images) Dickov questions defenders’ confidence in Kepa With Raya still a doubt, Kepa could be called upon to take his place once again. However, questions remain over whether Arsenal’s defenders will have the same level of confidence in him as they do in the former Brentford goalkeeper. Dickov shared his assessment of the situation, as quoted by the Metro , making it clear that he believes City could exploit the difference. ‘This is no disrespect to Kepa but I don’t think the back four will feel as comfortable with him back there knowing Raya isn’t behind them. City have to capitalise on that and put as much pressure on the back four and the goalkeeper as they can.’ His comments highlight the importance of Raya’s presence and the potential difficulties Arsenal could face if he misses the encounter. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Manchester City Monitoring In-Demand Grêmio Centre-Back Currently Breaking Through in Brazil
item.description: Manchester City Monitoring In-Demand Grêmio Centre-Back Currently Breaking Through in Brazil There has been no shortage of scrutiny of Manchester City's defending of late, with Enzo Maresca admitting only on Tuesday night in the aftermath of a 2-2 draw with Napoli that his side are conceding too many goals. Defensive reinforcements may well be on the horizon, though the latest player linked with a high-profile move the Premier League side is a young prospect rather than a marquee name. The latest defender a new report concerns has climbed onto the radar of Europe's elite clubs from a very unlikely starting point, and Enzo Maresca’s recruitment chiefs within the Etihad Stadium are far from his only suitor. Man City join growing list of admirers for Wallace That player is Wallace, the 21-year-old Grêmio defender whose displays have turned heads well beyond South America, and according to Brazilian journalist Fábio Vargas, as translated and relayed by Sport Witness , both Manchester City and AC Milan are monitoring the centre-back. Grêmio are said to have placed a €25 million/£20.9 million price tag on the defender's head. Of the two clubs mentioned as potential suitors, it is Milan who appear closest to acting for the player. The Serie A side are reportedly weighing up an official offer in the coming days while Manchester City are said to be keeping an eye on the situation rather than readying a bid of their own - at least for the time being. The two giants are not his only admirers with Brighton , who certainly know how to spot a talent in the South American market, reportedly had the defender flagged by scouts who were originally there to watch a different target. From second-tier substitute to European radar What makes the interest so striking is how little top-flight football Wallace has actually played. A product of CRB’s academy, Wallace has won three state championships with the second-division club, but could never nail down a regular starting berth, and had managed just six league games this season before Grêmio came calling in June. That switch became the biggest sale of an academy graduate in CRB’s history and since arriving, he has barely looked back having marked his Brazilian top-flight debut with a headed goal against São Paulo in August and swiftly making the position his own. Having now completing eight matches in a row while more seasoned defenders were rotated around him, Wallace has helped Grêmio reach the Copa do Brasil final and started Monday’s crucial 2-0 win over Santos that hauled the club clear of the relegation zone. Inexperience aside, Wallace's profile is an intriguing one; standing at 6’2” and an imposing, aggressive presence combining physicality and pace. Right-footed, but comfortable on either flank of central defence, he has also been deployed at right-back and defensive midfield. item.title: Alberto Puig on shock Marc Marquez retirement: 'I'm not surprised, it's the right decision'
item.description: Motorsport photo Honda MotoGP boss Alberto Puig says Marc Marquez's shock retirement is the correct decision for the 10-time motorcycle world champion. The HRC team manager, who worked with Marquez during his successful years at Honda - where he won six of his eight MotoGP crowns - said he wasn't surprised at the Spaniard calling time in the wake of his latest championship. Read Also: Marc Marquez announces immediate retirement from MotoGP in bombshell announcement "Frankly speaking, it's the correct decision at the correct time," Puig told the world feed immediately after the announcement. "He won the title again that nobody expected. He will be the greatest of all time for sure and he will go home and everybody will always remember him as the best rider ever. "So if he decided to go this way, it's because he understood he cannot continue performing at this level. The people that know him cannot imagine watching him race NOT to win, so I think it's sad in a way. "But in the other way it's super good. He had a super long and productive career and I don't think we will ever see again a guy like him." Puig was then asked if he was surprised by the announcement. "I'm not. Because he's a very clever guy and even though this type of decision is very complicated, Marc is what he is not only because he's a fast rider but also he's a very, very smart individual. Normally these types of people make the correct decisions at the right time." Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Asked what legacy Marc would leave, Puig said there was little need for deep analysis. "What he did is there. You can see what he did and the way he did it with all his injuries and with his passion for the sport. "We [Honda] were with Marc for many years but what he did is completely unreal. Sometimes you cannot even compare him with other good champions." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Marc Marquez to retire from MotoGP after record-equalling title win
item.description: Marc Marquez has announced he will retire from MotoGP at the end of the season after sealing a record-equalling eighth world championship . Ducati’s Marquez will bid farewell to the sport after the Valencia Grand Prix, the last race of the 2026 campaign, this Sunday. A statement from Ducati read: “It is official. Marc Marquez has decided to retire from MotoGP, and the 2026 Valencia Grand Prix will be his final race as a professional rider and with the Ducati Lenovo Team. “The Spanish rider will provide further details from 12:15pm onwards during a press conference at the Circuit Ricardo Tormo. Until then, no member of Ducati Corse will make any statements. Thank you.” We Made #H1STORY 🔴🏆 #ForzaDucati #ValenciaGP pic.twitter.com/Y0lW7ZAshJ — Ducati Corse (@ducaticorse) November 27, 2026 Marquez captured the MotoGP title last weekend in Portugal to go level with the great Giacomo Agostini on a record eight premier-class championships. He soaked in the glory in Lisbon, marking the occasion by ascending the staircase accompanied by the silhouette of a goat on the screen, a nod to his growing “Greatest of All ⁠Time” status, before receiving a golden commemorative helmet from Agostini himself. There were tears in the Ducati garage as well as in the stands when fans were told the Spaniard would be competing in his final race this weekend at ‌the Circuit Ricardo Tormo. Marc Marquez celebrates his eighth MotoGP title win (Reuters) "Thank you to everyone ​who's ⁠been part of the journey. I hope you've enjoyed it as ⁠much as I have. This will be ​my ⁠last race in MotoGP. ‌We made history," Marquez said in a video statement in the garage in ‌Valencia. Marquez won six titles with Honda in the space of seven years before making the switch to Ducati, with whom he has claimed back-to-back championships in the last two years. He had initially extended his contract with the Italian outfit until 2028 in June, but has now opted to call time on his legendary career. His title success this year came despite undergoing double surgery midway through the season on his right shoulder. Marquez has retired from MotoGP (Reuters) “I know that we are here celebrating a historic moment. I know how I suffered," said an emotional ⁠Marquez after the Portuguese Grand Prix. "I know that in the middle of the season, the fans believed more than I did. My people believed more than I did. But I kept pushing, I kept doing my best. "I said last year that it was a championship where I was at peace with myself. This one is for all the fans that believed in me from 2020 until now. So thanks to all of you, this is for all ‌of you."

item.title: 2027: Kwankwaso accuses Kano governor of plot to tarnish his image
item.description: Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has accused Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, of allegedly orchestrating a campaign to tarnish his reputation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso made the allegation in a statement issued on Friday, expressing concern over what he described as the alleged use of anti-corruption institutions, particularly the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), for political purposes. The former Kano State governor questioned the motives behind what he characterised as attempts to damage his public image, alleging that the anti-corruption agency was being drawn into political activities. He expressed concern that institutions established to fight corruption could be used to settle political scores, particularly as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. However, the allegations against Governor Yusuf remain claims by Kwankwaso and would require an independent response from the governor or his representatives. item.title: Levski Sofia fans hospitalised after violent clashes with Marseille supporters
item.description: Marseille head coach Bruno Genesio said “we are living through violent times” after five Levski Sofia fans were hospitalised following violent clashes before their Europa League encounter with the French side. Groups of supporters threw projectiles and flares and French outlet L’Equipe reported that there were Nazi salutes observed in the away section. Ten minutes before kick-off at the Stade Velodrome a group of Marseille fans broke through into the away stand, which housed around 500 fans. In the ensuing clashes five people, all Bulgarian, were injured and taken to hospital “with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder”, according to the Marseille police prefecture, while six others were treated on-site for more superficial injuries. The police force said there was “no information at this stage regarding any arrests”. Security were able to restore order and the game kicked off on time, although there were further incidents later on, particularly at half-time. Genesio said: “We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable.” Julio Velazquez, head coach of the Bulgarian domestic champions, said: “It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football.” The Bulgarian Football Union condemned the violence and said it had referred the incident to UEFA , calling for the harshest possible sanctions. It also demanded full cooperation and transparency from French authorities in investigating the attacks and identifying those responsible. There were violent clashes before kick-off (Reuters) Levski said the club's priority is the safety and well-being of its fans. A statement read: “What happened tonight is particularly alarming given the extraordinary security measures put in place by the French authorities, as well as the restrictions imposed on our travelling supporters—restrictions that the club had already formally contested with UEFA. “Despite the risks identified by the club prior to the match, the measures taken failed to provide adequate protection for our fans. This is completely unacceptable.” Both clubs condemned the violence (Reuters) Marseille also condemned the violence and said it is conducting “a thorough analysis of the circumstances in which these incidents took place.” Bulgarian President Iliana Yotova called for those responsible to be held accountable and Prime Minister Rumen Radev said he had spoken to French president Emmanuel Macron about the violence at a European summit in Brussels. A spokesperson for Macron’s office said: “He condemned in the strongest possible terms these acts of violence targeting Bulgarian supporters, which have no place in sport or in public spaces, and assured the Prime Minister that these acts would not go unpunished.” Marseille won the game 1-0, with Amine Gouiri scoring a 28th-minute penalty.

item.title: Tyson Fury's wife backtracks on schizophrenia claim
item.description: British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury faces Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11 (Fayez Nureldine) Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, has retracted her claim that the British heavyweight was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after he was crowned world champion in 2015. In clips promoting a Netflix documentary, the boxer spoke about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine's Wladimir Klitschko in Germany. Paris Fury said Tyson Fury had "mild schizophrenia" in an initial version of the documentary, which will be released on Friday. Netflix said it had worked to "update" the footage in light of her clarification. Fury, 38, is due to face Anthony Joshua in a long-awaited all-British showdown in Cardiff on December 11. Paris Fury's comments come after the British Boxing Board of Control indicated that it was investigating the comments, though Robert Smith, the board's general secretary, told the BBC it was "fairly confident" he would be cleared to fight Joshua. "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary," Paris said in a statement. "I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. "Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. "I'm so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we've received as a family." Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a break of nearly three years from boxing. His weight ballooned while he battled suicidal thoughts and drug and alcohol problems. Fury admitted hearing "voices in my mind" following his win, adding: "Words can't explain the darkness I was in. "I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I'd end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much." Fury became world heavyweight champion for a second time when he beat WBC champion Deontay Wilder in February 2020. Despite losing twice to Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, the only losses in his 39-fight professional career, Fury could become a three-time world champion when he takes on Joshua with the vacant WBA title set to be on the line. Netflix said in a statement: "Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson's official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch." jw/jkb/td

item.description: Marc Marquez's eight MotoGP titles have come between 2013 and 2026 [Getty Images] MotoGP champion Marc Marquez has said he will retire days after clinching a record-equalling eighth title. The 33-year-old Spaniard clinched the 2026 title in Portugal last weekend and will end his professional career after the final race of the season in Valencia. The Ducati rider's latest triumph puts him level with Giacomo Agostini and one clear of modern great Valentino Rossi. "Thank you to everyone who's been part of the journey," he said. "I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have." More to follow. Is Marquez MotoGP's greatest of all time?

item.title: Michael Olise ruled out of Bayern's trip to Hamburg
item.description: Michael Olise ruled out of Bayern's trip to Hamburg Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Michael Olise will miss Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Hamburger SV. The French winger also sat out Wednesday's 2-1 Champions League defeat to LOSC Lille after suffering a bruised foot in last week's 1-1 draw with 1. FC Köln. “Michael [Olise] won't play,” Kompany confirmed at a press conference on Friday. "Everything else is open. The priority is the team, not individual players. We've got four games - including Wednesday - in nine days. We need to use our squad - and it is how it is at the moment. Everything's open, but we still have the same demands." In addition to Olise, Bayern will also be without Harry Kane, Ismaël Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer due to injury. “The reality is that we're missing 130 goals in the squad. But we still have the same demands. We want to win. We didn't do that, which doesn't feel good. At the moment we only have one superstar, which is the team. My focus is on this superstar,” Kompany said. On the positive side, Kompany believes Bayern's current injury crisis presents an opportunity for young, unproven players such as Noah Codjo-Evora and Tim Binder to step up, make their mark and gain valuable first-team experience. “What can this period mean for a club? We can give two or three players some experience who could prove vital at the end of the season. That can’t happen if the guys don’t get the playing time they need. We’ve still factored them into our plans in this situation. We know that something like what we’re currently experiencing can always happen. That’s why their role will very quickly become very important,” Kompany said. "[Noah] Codjo-Evora has often been injured, but he’s a very well-rounded player. He’s very precise with his first touch, is ambidextrous, can finish, and has strength. You can see where he’s capable of going in the future. Tim Binder is quick in one-v-one situations. They’ve been training with us for a long time now, but they all still need to develop. "However, we hope they can play without pressure. If they don’t perform well now, it doesn’t mean it’s all over. They’re young players who are helping us and who might be able to help us even more at the end of the season, because they’re gaining experience now."

item.title: Marc Marquez to end storied MotoGP career after eighth world crown
item.description: Marc Marquez won his eighth MotoGP title last weekend (FILIPE AMORIM) Marc Marquez will bring the curtain down on his MotoGP career after this weekend's season-ending Grand Prix in Valencia, following a historic season in which he won his record-equalling eighth title. Spaniard Marquez claimed his eighth title in the premier class of motorcycling last weekend at the Portuguese Grand Prix, his second in as many years for Italian team Ducati. "It is official. @marcmarquez93 has decided to retire from @motogp, and the 2026 Valencia Grand Prix will be his final race as a professional rider and with the #DucatiLenovoTeam," said Ducati on social media on Friday. Marquez then relayed his own message, via a video recorded on the paddock at the Ricardo Tormo circuit, with a series of placards held up to the camera. "Thank you to everyone who's been part of this journey, I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have," said Marquez. "This will be my last race in MotoGP. We made history." Marquez's latest success pulled him level with Italian great Giacomo Agostini who won his titles between 1966 and 1975. He also overtakes his great rival Valentino Rossi, who won seven MotoGP titles, although the swashbuckling Italian has 89 individual race wins in the top category to Marquez's 80. The latest triumph is even more remarkable given the 33-year-old's injury and crash-blighted campaign in which he had to wait until the eighth race in Hungary on June 7 before claiming his first win. Marquez suffered a flat tyre in the season-opener in Thailand in March, fell at the Spanish GP in Jerez and again at the French GP where he picked up a foot fracture which ruled him out of the following race, the Catalan GP. Making his comeback at the Italian GP in Mugello he trailed Bezzecchi by a massive 102 points in early June just weeks after undergoing foot surgery on top of a previous operation on his injured shoulder. But once he got rolling he roared into a regular winning run with seven Grand Prix and 10 sprint race victories in all this season. td/ach

item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Vice-President Kashim Shettima on Friday led prominent personalities to the second-term inauguration of Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, held at the Osogbo Township Stadium. Adeleke was re-elected governor on August 15, 2026, defeating the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, by more than 60,000 votes. The inauguration, which was ongoing at the time of filing this report, attracted several political figures, including APC National Leader, Chief Bisi Akande; former Senate President, Bukola Saraki; and former APC National Secretary, Senator Iyiola Omisore. Also in attendance were former Osun State Deputy Governor, Benedict Alabi; the Olubadan of Ibadan, Oba Rashidi Ladoja; the Soun of Ogbomoso, Oba Ghandi Olaoye; and the Ataoja of Osogbo, Oba Jimoh Olanipekun, among other traditional rulers. Captains of industry, academics, politicians and other dignitaries were also present at the ceremony. item.title: Franck Haise in danger of being sacked at Rennes
item.description: Franck Haise in danger of being sacked at Rennes Stade Rennais, who have just one win in their last eight games in all competitions, are now in a state of crisis. Several important members of staff could depart the club as a result, as per a report from Foot Mercato. Thursday night’s loss to NEC Nijmegen could cost Franck Haise his job. The Frenchman, who earlier in his managerial career had managed Rennes’ youth side, joined midway through last season and guided them to UEFA Europa League qualification. His side started this season strongly, too, but the wheels have come off. Their only win in their last eight games came against an RC Strasbourg Alsace side also in crisis. The club have dropped to ninth in Ligue 1, whilst they have just one win in the UEFA Europa League, against OFI Crete. Foot Mercato understands that, internally, fractures are starting to show and Haise may have lost some of the Rennes dressing room, including some of its key components. His job is, therefore, threatened. Haise may not be the only potential victim. Club president Arnaud Pouille is also under threat. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: 2027: Emerging opposition coalition comprises displaced politicians — Lagos APC
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has criticised ongoing merger and coalition talks among opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general elections, describing the emerging alliance as an association of “internally displaced politicians” driven by personal grievances rather than a coherent vision for governance. The Lagos APC spokesman, Seye Oladejo, who made the remark on Friday, questioned the ideological consistency and sincerity of the political actors seeking to unite against President Bola Tinubu in 2027. According to Oladejo, the emerging alliance comprises former power brokers, ex-officeholders and frustrated aspirants who previously benefited from or helped shape the same political establishments they now criticise. He maintained that the coalition lacked a unified policy framework on critical national issues, including economic management, energy reforms, foreign exchange policy and national security. “What is being marketed to Nigerians as a formidable opposition coalition increasingly looks like an assembly of politically displaced persons, disgruntled power brokers, frustrated presidential aspirants and former beneficiaries of the very political establishments they now denounce,” the Lagos APC spokesman said. Reacting to another round of opposition consultations scheduled for Monday, Oladejo dismissed the repeated meetings as “political motion without movement”. He argued that bringing prominent political figures together under one roof did not automatically translate into grassroots electoral structures or administrative competence. Oladejo further contended that opposition rhetoric had become excessively focused on opposing Tinubu rather than presenting a credible alternative blueprint for governance. While acknowledging that the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had brought difficult adjustments for households and businesses, the Lagos APC maintained that the 2027 election would be determined by verifiable performance records, policy continuity and organisational strength rather than what it described as a “coalition of grievances”. item.title: ‘Never been a more clear year for the Bills to finally win the Super Bowl,’ says RG3
item.description: Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are now 10-1 for the season after a Thanksgiving win over the Kansas City Chiefs and Robert Griffin III is positive about their Super Bowl prospects. It was not a high-scoring game and Josh Allen, in particular, struggled to have a huge impact, only managing 81 passing yards and no touchdowns compared to 174 yards for Patrick Mahomes. But all that really matters for Buffalo is they secured a 13-10 victory and are currently the top team in the NFL. Whether their regular season success translates over into the playoffs remains to be seen. But Griffin now thinks that there’s ‘never been a more clear year’ for the Bills to finally win a Super Bowl. Robert Griffin III suggests Buffalo Bills may finally win Super Bowl in 2027 Taking to X/Twitter, he stated: “Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills are 10-1 and win on a walk off FG after the Chiefs mismanage the last moments of the game. There has never been a more clear year for the Bills to finally win the Super Bowl. This is the team who can do it.” With six games left to play, the Bills are well on track to set a new regular season record, having previously never won more than 13 games in one year. This is great news for the team, of course, but they will be more concerned with what happens from January onwards. They have not made it to the Super Bowl since 1993 and have come up short in all four of their appearances. Allen, on paper, should be good enough to help them return to the grandest stage in early 2027, but his recent form is becoming a concern. He had a couple of off games in the lead-up to Thanksgiving and was largely neutralised by the Chiefs on November 26. His postseason record is 8–7 but he has come up short against Mahomes on four occasions. item.title: Barcelona set clear condition for out-of-favour defender’s potential January departure – report
item.description: Barcelona set clear condition for out-of-favour defender’s potential January departure – report According to SPORT , Barcelona are willing to consider Alejandro Balde’s departure during the January transfer window, but only if they can secure a suitable defensive replacement first. The left-back has lost prominence under Hansi Flick, attracting interest from several major European clubs, yet the Catalan giants do not want to weaken their defence midway through the season without having another option in place. Reinforcement before exits Barring his start against Sabah FK earlier this season, Balde has barely featured prominently for Barcelona this season. In all, the 23-year-old La Masia graduate has only made six appearances across competitions, racking up a measly 188 minutes of action, giving way to speculations over his future. The defender, who suffered a minor ankle injury against Sabah , is said to be open to the idea of an exit in January if he cannot get regular opportunities at Barcelona. However, the Blaugrana sporting department wants to bring in a left-footed centre-back who could provide cover at full-back when required or allow Gerard Martin to feature more regularly on the left before parting ways with Balde. No longer a regular at Barcelona. (Photo by Daniela Porcelli/Getty Images) Although moving their homegrown defender on could free up salary space and help Barcelona pursue other targets, they are unwilling to rush into a decision without first addressing their defensive needs. AC Milan and Juventus interested Balde’s agent, Jorge Mendes, is already working on possible destinations, with Italy emerging as one of the strongest possibilities. AC Milan and Juventus are both interested in the Barcelona academy graduate. The Rossoneri see the 23-year-old defender’s valuation as too steep for January and are exploring the possibility of a paid loan deal with an option to buy that could become mandatory if certain conditions are met. Milan also have some concerns about Balde’s €6 million salary and that would also need to be negotiated. Their strong ties with Mendes could help facilitate smooth talks. As for Juventus, manager Luciano Spalletti is also eager to strengthen his options on the left side of the defence and sees the Barcelona outcast as a good fit. No shortage of interest in Balde. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) However, the Bianconeri would also prefer only a loan move for the player rather than a permanent transfer. Liverpool, Manchester United and Tottenham in the Premier League are also keeping track of developments ahead of the winter window. Barcelona, for their part, would prefer a permanent transfer for a fee of around €30 million at least. However, they could also consider a loan with an option to buy as long as the arrangement frees up the entirety of Balde’s salary. Donaldson handled his biggest workload as a Saint with 48% of routes and 44% of snaps, so perhaps he might be taking over the Kamara role? All that said, Etienne isn’t out of the woods yet, but he’s increasingly more startable than he was before. Fantasy Advice: Neither Kamara nor Donaldson is startable, but Etienne is a low-end flex play against the Bengals if his Week 11 utilization holds. WR Jordyn Tyson Just when you thought you could trust Tyson after a 13-target, 11-reception game in Week 10, he (or maybe head coach Kellen Moore deserves more of the blame) pulls the rug out from under you with a one-target, one-catch game for six yards. His route participation also precipitously dropped, from 72% in Week 10 to just 42%. Week 10 was all Tyson; this past week was all Olave. (Let’s find a happy medium here, people!) I still think Tyson is going to matter for fantasy managers and the real-life NFL team for the rest of this season, but it seems the runout is going to be more gradual than expecting his Week 10 line to be the norm. item.title: GTA in Istanbul? Meet the game developers bringing virtual crime chaos to their home cities
item.description: From Helsinki to Istanbul, independent developers are putting Grand Theft Auto-style action on their home streets, and without billion-dollar budgets. They tell us how they do it Like most kids who shouldn’t have been playing Grand Theft Auto III in 2001, Eamonn Swayah imagined a version of Rockstar Games’ groundbreaking criminal sandbox set in his own back yard. In his case, that was a Manchester council estate, complete with local accents, driving on the left, and plenty of ways to hustle. He didn’t know it, but swapping the game’s facsimile of early 2000s New York City for a different setting was an idea he shared with many watchful game developers. Rockstar’s 3D open world template, it turned out, could be plonked in just about any location, so long as it had people and enough cars to run them over with. After GTA III attracted immense commercial success (and controversy), dozens of copycats and spiritual sequels hit the market throughout the 00s and 2010s. Gamers had a pithy name for them: “GTA clones”. Continue reading...
