item.title: Real Madrid defender not thinking about January exit despite uncertain future – report
item.description: Real Madrid defender not thinking about January exit despite uncertain future – report Among all the signings Real Madrid have made in the recent past, Trent Alexander-Arnold has perhaps been the most disappointing one. The Englishman came in with the reputation of being one of the world’s best right-backs, having won the Champions League and the Premier League at Liverpool. But 18 months into his Real Madrid career, the defender has yet to establish himself as a first-team regular at the club, even after the summer exit of Dani Carvajal. This has led to question marks over Trent’s future, with Chelsea and Manchester United among the clubs interested in his services. Trent not thinking about an exit Trent has fallen behind Federico Valverde in the pecking order. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) However, a recent report from The Athletic has indicated that Trent is not thinking about leaving Real Madrid in the upcoming January transfer window. The English international is not too keen on leaving Santiago Bernabeu just 18 months after joining the club and is trying to do everything he can to establish himself as a first-team starter. This comes against the backdrop of calls for Trent to return to Liverpool, with club legend Steven Gerrard endorsing the idea recently. But it appears the right-back has no desire to give up just yet and wants to fight for his place in the starting eleven. Can Trent become a starter at Real Madrid? Trent’s future at Real Madrid looks uncertain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) It is clear that Jose Mourinho has liked what he has seen from Federico Valverde and considers the Uruguayan international his first-choice right-back this season. As for Trent, he has struggled to perform even when given limited opportunities, with the Englishman most recently failing to make an impression against Celta Vigo. This doesn’t bode well for Trent’s chances, especially given the fact that he also has competition from Denzel Dumfries. However, the month of December could be interesting for Mourinho, who has embraced more rotations in recent weeks in an attempt to keep his first-choice players fit and healthy for the important matches. Between now and Christmas, Real Madrid are slated to play six matches, and it won’t be surprising to see Trent appear in at least a few of them, which in turn, could be his opportunity to impress Mourinho, heading into the second half of the season.

item.title: Serie A Preview: Sassuolo vs Napoli – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: Serie A Preview: Sassuolo vs Napoli – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Sassuolo welcome Napoli to the Mapei Stadium on Sunday afternoon, with both sides desperate to get their Serie A campaigns back on track. The hosts have endured a miserable start to the season, collecting just eight points from their opening 12 matches to slip into the relegation zone. Meanwhile, Napoli have struggled to find their rhythm under under-fire Massimiliano Allegri and are already nine points behind fourth-placed Milan. The Partenopei will be keen to build on their recent improvement and close the gap on the European qualification places, while Roberto D’Aversa faces the difficult task of stopping Sassuolo’s alarming decline. The visitors have dominated this fixture in recent years, making them favorites to claim maximum points despite mounting injury problems. Match Preview Sassuolo Sassuolo have endured a nightmare start to their Serie A campaign, registering just two victories from their opening 12 fixtures while losing six consecutive league matches ahead of Sunday’s encounter. Their latest setback came against Genoa, who secured a comfortable 2-0 win on D’Aversa’s touchline debut. The Neroverdi dismissed Alberto Aquilani after a disappointing run and appointed D’Aversa in a desperate attempt to revive their survival hopes. However, the former Lecce manager faces an uphill battle, with his new side already sitting in the relegation zone and lamenting one of the division’s most vulnerable defences. Sassuolo have conceded 31 goals in 12 league outings, averaging more than 2.5 per match, while their opponents have registered a league-high number of shots on target against them. Their defensive frailties have proved particularly costly in recent weeks, with the Neroverdi conceding at least twice in four of their last five Serie A matches. Nevertheless, Mapei Stadium remains their strongest source of encouragement, having collected seven of their eight league points on home soil. Domenico Berardi will once again shoulder much of the attacking responsibility, with the Italian winger having scored three times against Napoli in previous meetings, all at home. Napoli Napoli have also fallen short of expectations this season, with Allegri struggling to find the consistency required to mount a sustained Scudetto challenge. The four-time Italian champions have amassed 18 points from their opening 12 fixtures. As a result, they are well outside the European qualification spots and already facing considerable pressure. However, the Partenopei have shown signs of improvement since the November international break, edging past Torino 1-0 last weekend before producing a promising performance against Manchester City in the Champions League. Napoli took the lead twice at the Etihad Stadium but eventually settled for a 2-2 draw, demonstrating they can still compete against Europe’s strongest sides. item.title: Russell fires another shot at Verstappen over his on-track behaviour
item.description: George Russell has claimed that few other Formula 1 drivers would have attempted the same move as Max Verstappen during their controversial practice encounter at the Las Vegas Grand Prix , insisting that his reaction would have been identical regardless of who was behind the wheel. The two drivers reignited their long-standing rivalry in Las Vegas after making contact during the final practice session while preparing for their respective flying laps. The incident resulted in a five-place grid penalty for Verstappen, although the Dutchman subsequently inherited pole position following Kimi Antonelli's own grid penalty. Tensions between the two championship contenders escalated further over the course of the weekend, with Verstappen delivering a scathing assessment of Russell after securing victory on Sunday, claiming that the Mercedes driver was “so far below my level”. Russell addressed those remarks upon arriving in Qatar, describing Verstappen's comments as unnecessary. However, the Briton also suggested that the Red Bull driver's behaviour had come at the expense of other drivers in recent weeks. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Speaking during the FIA press conference ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Russell was subsequently asked whether his practice encounter with Verstappen in Las Vegas represented the straw that broke the camel's back, following a gradual build-up of frustration over the preceding rounds. The Mercedes driver insisted that his reaction stemmed from the circumstances surrounding the incident rather than the identity of the driver involved. “I think what happened in practice, I think how I responded on track would have been the same if it was any driver, because you do know if you're going into the last corner preparing for your lap, if somebody does overtake you into that corner, your next lap is screwed.” Russell went on to explain the dilemma he faced when Verstappen attempted to overtake him, arguing that conceding the position would effectively have compromised his next flying lap. “You either have a decision just to try and retake the position and start your lap like normal, or just accept you're going to lose that next lap because you're too close to the car in front. That's that.” Russell singles out Verstappen over controversial Vegas move The latest disagreement between Russell and Verstappen comes almost two years after their highly publicised fallout at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, when a qualifying incident and the subsequent stewards' hearing triggered a fierce war of words between the pair. While Russell maintained that his response in Las Vegas was not influenced by their turbulent history, the Briton suggested that few of his fellow competitors would have put him in that position in the first place. “As I said, I would have reacted the same way on track if there was any other driver, but I don't think many other drivers would go for that move in the first place. But it's fine. That's how he races, and t

item.title: Beat Michigan! Put ball in Jeremiah Smith's hand to send him out with 'gold pants' | Opinion
item.description: Colorado resident Kelly Immel earned a 1992 bachelor’s degree in journalism from Ohio State University. ’Twas the night ‘fore The Game and as I ready for bed, I reflect on the season as I lay down my head. The losses they hurt, and they had us all miffed. But all is not lost, we’ve been given a gift. He wears number four and we got to see, the greatest in history to represent THE. Coach Day nearly fainted and the stars did align, When the kid from Miami on the dots he did sign. We did not know then what he really could do, When he strapped on his pads and walked into The Shoe. In his first year against Michigan State, He made such a catch that predicted his fate. Third and Jeremiah will go down in our lore as one of the best to set up a score. And the touchdown last year in The Game with the snow gave us a grin just beginning to grow. There were snatches he made that left us in awe, and most of those grabs were made with one paw. Kelly Immel: OSU won for nameless members of Buckeye Nation like me. I am still grinning The receptions kept coming and opponents did try, but it was too hard to stop him as he leapt towards the sky. As the season wore on and they fed him the ball, a new goal was then set, JJ 4 It All. So many records he’ll have, when it’s all said and done, but the last one he wants is to be 2-1. He’s the GOAT on the field, and everyone knows. What we hope will come next is the strike of a pose. That trophy of bronze, we have such a slew. We’ve got Vic, we’ve got Les, we’ve got Archie with two. With Hopalong, Eddie , and Troy as of late, and JJ up next , now that would make eight. The next victory is ours and to ensure it is done, put the ball in his hands, and The Game is sure won. It will be his last year in the Scarlet and Grey, but if we beg and we plead, do you think he would stay? Letters: Buckeyes labeled Big Ten's most disappointing team. Whose head should roll? The stage is now set, he gave us his all. Have I mentioned it yet, to just throw him the ball? The joy that he gave us, we can never repay. We love him, we thank him, what else can we say? We wish him great things, and our hearts does he hold. Let’s send him out right with some pants made of gold. Kelly Immel earned a 1992 bachelor’s degree in journalism from The Ohio State University. She currently cheers for the Buckeyes from Breckenridge, Colorado . Online Form - Columbus Dispatch Letter to the Editor This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Beat Michigan! Put ball in Jeremiah Smith's hand to send him out with 'gold pants' | Opinion

item.title: Wanderers approved for home stadium leasehold
item.description: The Wanderers have played at Meadowbank since 2018, after it was refurbished [Getty Images] The proposed transfer of ownership of Meadowbank Stadium from Surrey County Football Association to Dorking Wanderers Football Club has been approved by Mole Valley District Council. The Wanderers have played there since 2018 after it was refurbished. It had previously been home to Dorking FC prior to their disbanding. The club said it "marks a significant milestone" following several years of hard work to reach this point. Completion of the lease arrangements remains subject to approval from the East Surrey Shadow Authority executive, according to the district council, due to local government reorganisation in the county. A club spokesperson said: "Taking responsibility for Meadowbank will give the club greater control over its future, creating opportunities to develop additional income streams and build on the stadium's role as a hub for the community." The acquisition is being supported by new co-owners Frank Villares and Debra Tucker. The pair recently bought a stake in the sixth-tier club , which was formed and is owned and managed by Marc White. The club said it has provided the funding necessary to complete the deal. Villares said: "Getting involved in Dorking Wanderers was about several things for Debra and me. "Of course we want to see success on the pitch and we're sure we will, but creating income streams for the club is crucial. "I'd like to thank everyone at Mole Valley District Council and Surrey County Football Association for their cooperation and support throughout this process. "We're looking forward to taking over the operation of Meadowbank and building on what is already a fantastic hub for the community." item.title: 2027 Election:​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​‍‌‌​‍‍‌​ INEC procures 57,000 new BVAS devices
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission has procured 57,000 new BVAS for the 2027 general elections. Prof. Amupitan disclosed this on Thursday during a sensitisation seminar by the Diocese of Abuja, Anglican Communion, on Civil and Political Education with the theme “Why Your Vote Still Matters” Represented by the Deputy Director, Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Wilfred Ifogah, Prof. Amupitan said that the commission had also reduced the threshold from 1,250 to 850 voters per machine and cleaned the register through biometric audit. He said that with 51 days to the Jan. 16, 2027, presidential and National Assembly elections, civic responsibility must not be outsourced. Amupitan said INEC would on Saturday conduct a nationwide mock accreditation exercise in two polling units per ward to test upgrades ahead of 2027. According to him, over 10.77 million new registrants were recorded during the Continuous Voter Registration, while over 1.6 million invalid records were removed, bringing the verified register to over 100 million voters, including 232,658 persons with disabilities. He said INEC had also upgraded its Result Viewing Portal, IReV, with automated checks for over-voting and arithmetic consistency on Form EC8A before transmission. The INEC boss urged citizens to resist vote buying, divisive politics and inflammatory language, noting that Sections 95, 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026 prescribe stiff penalties for electoral violence and hate speech. Also speaking, a legal practitioner, Mr Emeka Etiaba, SAN, said over-judicialisation of elections was eroding public confidence. Etiaba said trust is earned, not commanded, stressing that INEC and the judiciary must deliver credible processes in 2027 to restore confidence. He noted that technicalities, poor petition drafting and non-justiciable innovations often deny determination of cases on merit, leaving a few judges to decide outcomes involving thousands of voters. He said innovations such as AI validation on IReV, though laudable administratively, must be backed by law to be enforceable in court. Speaking at the event, the Primate of the Church of Nigeria, Anglican Communion, Most Rev. Henry Ndukuba, urged Nigerians, especially youths, to actively participate in the 2027 general elections. According to him, their votes remain critical to deepening democracy and national development. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the seminar is part of activities marking the 37th anniversary of the diocese and Carnival for Christ 2026. Ndukuba said the church organised the seminar to sensitise citizens on their civic responsibility ahead of the polls, and the 2027 electioneering campaigns were already underway, with general elections scheduled for January 2027. He said the church deemed it important to engage stakeholders in the electoral process to educate citizens on the need to make informed decisions. “Most of our citizens

item.title: ‘Just an Embarrassment,’ ‘What a Joke’ — Ex-NFL Scout Blasts NBC’s ‘God Awful’ Mike Tomlin Segment on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy Controversy
item.description: ‘Just an Embarrassment,’ ‘What a Joke’ — Ex-NFL Scout Blasts NBC’s ‘God Awful’ Mike Tomlin Segment on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy Controversy With the Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy controversy dominating the NFL conversation, NBC saw an opportunity to set up a Thanksgiving interview with former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin. NBC devoted most of the Chiefs-Bills halftime broadcast to a taped Mike Tomlin interview instead of the Goo Goo Dolls’ live performance, airing only a brief portion of the band’s set. Former NFL scout John Middlekauff criticized the decision, saying NBC’s poor editing failed to capture the moment while Rodgers was discussing the controversy live. John Middlekauff Slams NBC’s Production Choices The Thanksgiving broadcast arrived at the height of one of the most dramatic midseason implosions in recent NFL memory. After back-to-back losses, offensive stagnation, and mounting friction over play-calling, head coach McCarthy benched Rodgers on Tuesday for backup Mason Rudolph. Rodgers ranked 29th in PFN’s QB Impact Score with a grade of 67.1 — his worst season grade in his career. Rodgers did not take the decision quietly. During a live appearance on ‘The Pat McAfee Show’, the veteran quarterback openly criticized McCarthy’s leadership, accusing him of falling asleep in meetings, missing meetings and walkthroughs, and mistakenly breaking down a halftime huddle with ‘1-2-3 Packers!’ Within hours of Rodgers’ interview, the Steelers released the future Hall of Famer. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Against that backdrop of real-time chaos, Middlekauff took to X to blast NBC’s decision to air a chopped-up, pre-recorded segment rather than matching the immediacy of the moment. “Rodgers going raw and real on the situation live while NBC gets Mike – cuts up a taped interview (god awful editing) is just an embarrassment to the consumer. What a joke,” Middlekauff wrote . He also made it clear that his criticism was directed at NBC rather than Tomlin. “And I’m not blaming Tomlin. That’s 100% on the network. It’s either a live normal convo or we just go listen to Iris,” he added. Tomlin Delivers Blunt Assessment of Steelers Controversy Despite NBC’s editing criticism, Tomlin’s comments offered a rare look at how he viewed the turmoil inside his former locker room. “To see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are the kinds of things that run counter culture to professional football,” Tomlin said . He also offered a blunt description of the situation unfolding in Pittsburgh. “I’m upset about it,” Tomlin said. “It’s a dumpster fire, and I don’t say it in a judgmental way. I’ve presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Tomlin did not speculate on whether Steelers owner Art Rooney II, who publicly backed McCarthy on Thursday, would seek his advice about the situation. item.title: Steve Kerr makes ‘Steph-dependent’ admission about Warriors amid two-game winning streak
item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors head coach explained how they’ve made a few changes after realising the team was relying too much on superstar Stephen Curry. When the season began, nobody expected the Golden State Warriors to be competitive this season. However, a stellar start to the season by Stephen Curry and the emergence of Yaxel Lendeborg saw them get off to an 8-4 start. As if things were going too well, though, Curry was struck down by injury. The team has understandably struggled since Curry has been out with an abdominal tear. They have a 2-4 record, averaging just 104.3 points per game in the games he has missed this year. Their last two results have brought back some positivity, though, with wins against the Celtics and the Kings. Head coach Steve Kerr has revealed that he has been working to minimise the effect of not having Steph. Steve Kerr says Warriors realised their offensive dependence on Steph Curry and have ‘tweaked’ the offence to change that If the Warriors can stay competitive, the return of Curry and Jimmy Butler along with a potential trade later in the season could completely change how they are viewed. For that, they must continue to win as much as they can in their superstar’s absence. The Warriors’ problem has always been that their superstars are so unique, that the system tends to fail in their absence. But it seems the coach has identified it this time, as he recently explained. “We’ve recognized that the way we were running our offense was too Steph-dependent, and so we’ve tweaked a few things, and I want to qualify that by saying whatever we run, Steph’s going to score,” Kerr said on the Tom Tolbert Show. “It doesn’t matter what we run for Steph, but it matters for everybody else, and so the way some of the nuances within our offense we needed to tweak, and we’ve made some changes this week, and hopefully we’ll be better for it long term.” After a tough matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers in their next game, the Warriors will face the Clippers and the Jazz in what they should consider to be winnable games. If the tweaks work, maybe they can keep their heads above water and set the stage for Curry’s eventual return to the court, which hopefully isn’t too far off. item.title: Ferrari Civil War Twist: Charles Leclerc Linked With $80 Million Aston Martin Move
item.description: Charles Leclerc has been linked with a shock move to Aston Martin after the constant drama at Ferrari. (Source: MEGA) Ferrari’s feud between its own drivers just got bigger. Last Saturday, Charles Leclerc tried an ambitious move on the inside at Turn 7; the cars made contact and Hamilton spun. Now a fresh report says Leclerc’s camp has had a word with Aston Martin about a deal worth around €70m (£59m) per year, which works out to roughly $80 million. The timing couldn’t be worse for team principal Fred Vasseur , who had already run out of patience with Lewis Hamilton and Leclerc. “For the second time in three races, something unacceptable has happened between our drivers, and this cannot continue,” Vasseur said. “Charles knows he made a mistake and apologised, but that doesn’t change the result.” Charles Leclerc has been linked with Aston Martin a couple of times in the recent past. (Source: MEGA) GPFans reported the rumor Friday, based on a story from Italian outlet Tuttosport . That story says Leclerc’s manager, son of former Ferrari and FIA chief Jean Todt, Nicolas Todt, has made contact with the Aston Martin team regarding a shock move to replace Fernando Alonso once the 45-year-old retires. The pitch reportedly includes working with design guru Adrian Newey . Treat this as talk for now, not a done deal. Leclerc only signed a new Ferrari deal this year until 2030, and GP Fans said it reached out to his management for comment. They haven’t received any so far. Las Vegas Crash Leaves Ferrari Fuming The warning signs showed up on the radio before the collision happened. “Careful with the squeezing because it’s not going to end well,” Leclerc said, while Hamilton asked the team: “Can you tell him to back the f*** off because I’m trying to catch the guys ahead.” The recent clashes between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have become a headache for Ferrari. (Source: MEGA) The stewards ruled that Leclerc had come from too far behind his teammate, which meant Hamilton had no obligation to leave him room on the inside. Leclerc took a 10-second penalty and dropped to 10th, while Hamilton fought back to seventh. Vasseur didn’t hold back. “The issue is once again it’s unacceptable. It’s a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors,” he said. As for his post-race chat with Leclerc: “It was not a discussion; I spoke!” Leclerc told Sky Sports F1 that “I just felt quite embarrassed for the team in general. We’ll review.” Still, he didn’t fully back down. “I felt there was a place to get there without taking too much risk,” he said, before admitting, “I probably underestimated the vision that Lewis had at that point.” Charles Leclerc was summoned by Fred Vasseur during the cooldown lap in Las Vegas. item.title: British social security system techies yank services offline following 'cyber incident'
item.description: The UK's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has taken some services offline after detecting a "cyber incident," but says regular benefit and pension payments are unaffected. The department announced the precautionary shutdown on Friday morning. "We have taken some DWP online services offline as a precaution after we identified a cyber incident affecting our systems," it said. "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre (GC3) to investigate and to bring services back online as quickly as possible and to minimize any disruption. "Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal. If an online service you need is unavailable, please try again later. As always, we will never message you to ask for bank details or ask you to click on links." The Register contacted both the DWP and NCSC for more information. The DWP declined to comment beyond the statement issued publicly. GC3 coordinates responses to incidents affecting government. The Government Cyber Unit leads the wider Government Cyber Action Plan, backed by more than £210 million. It is led by the government CISO, Bella Powell. Officials have not commented on any of the usual details one would expect from a cyber incident disclosure, including the specific services that were downed, when they are expected to return, or whether any data is thought to be compromised, even at this early stage. The UK government has also been criticized recently for investing heavily in AI cyber defenses, while the issue of legacy and aging IT continues to be neglected in the background. It announced at the end of October that it was throwing £130 million at AI cyber defense technology , as part of a wider £600 million cross-government AI spending spree announced by the Treasury. ExfilSquad recently claimed to have stolen around 607,000 records from the Department for Education and another 114,000 from the Police National Legal Database. ®

item.title: Questions about Tinubu’s identity come up anytime he’s about to win election — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed renewed questions about President Bola Tinubu’s background and identity, saying the controversies resurface whenever the president is on the verge of winning an election. Fashola described the questions as needless distractions, insisting that Tinubu had met the constitutional requirements to contest the presidency and that Nigerians had already settled the matter through their votes. He said the controversy had persisted for more than two decades but had not stopped Tinubu from winning elections, expressing confidence that the president would secure another victory in 2027. Fashola spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to questions about the perceived secrecy surrounding Tinubu’s background and identity. “I think that these matters have carried on for all of 20-something years. So, every time he’s at the threshold of winning an election, these issues come, and you know what always happens: he wins,” he said. “So history is about to repeat itself again. He’s going to win. These are needless distractions. They don’t answer a fundamental question. And I’ve said about minimum qualification. He has met it,” the former governor added. Fashola questioned the relevance of the controversies to Nigerians, saying opposition politicians should focus on issues that would improve the lives of citizens rather than repeatedly raising questions about Tinubu’s background. “The question I will focus upon if I were those fragmented opposition is how does this help the people whose mandate I want? It doesn’t help them,” he said. The former minister of works also argued that some of the issues had previously been subjected to legal proceedings and investigations, including during the 1999 political period and the last presidential election. Drawing on his experience as a legal practitioner, Fashola said there was a need to allow an end to prolonged disputes, invoking the legal principle that litigation must eventually come to a conclusion. “I believe parts of this were litigated in the last election. They were litigated in 1999. It was the subject of a House investigation in that period. You keep referring to my other life as a legal practitioner, there’s a principle in that life. There’s something we say, a principle that there must be an end to litigation. It’s enough,” he said. Fashola said Nigerians had moved on from the controversy, citing Tinubu’s victory in the 2023 presidential election as evidence, and predicted that voters would reaffirm their position in 2027. “They pursue it at their own choice, but I think the Nigerian people have left that subject behind. They have left it behind with their votes in 2023. They will reaffirm it in 2027,” he said. The post Questions about Tinubu’s identity come up anytime he’s about to win election — Fashola appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mock Accreditation: Sanwo-Olu Cancels November Environmental Sanitation Exercise
item.description: Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has cancelled the November edition of the state’s monthly environmental sanitation exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28, 2026. The development was disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Public Affairs, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Kunle Adeshina. The decision was taken to allow the smooth conduct of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise scheduled for the same day. In an updated statement issued on Friday and signed by the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Gaji Tajudeen, the governor said the INEC exercise would hold between 8:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m. This file photo shows an ad hoc official of INEC accrediting a voter with a BVAS machine. The mock exercise is expected to cover two polling units in each of Nigeria’s 8,838 Registration Areas. According to the statement, the governor considered it necessary to cancel the sanitation exercise to prevent any disruption to the commencement of the mock accreditation, which is also scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. The state government, however, urged residents to keep their surroundings clean regularly rather than wait for the monthly sanitation exercise. item.title: New Scientist Book Club: How urine changed the course of human history
item.description: A detail from Joseph Wright’s 1771 painting The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus, showing Henning Brand in 1669 Science History Images/Alamy Imagine you could boil the development of science down to a single ingredient. A magical, mystical compound that transformed human history. Of course, science doesn’t work that way; even if breakthroughs shift the paradigm of our understanding, discovery doesn’t progress like a tech tree in a computer game, but as an interweaving tapestry of complementary and competing ideas and experimentation. Theories can bubble under the surface for centuries, overlooked because of politics or failure to realise their implications, while innovations can emerge from taking an idea in one industry and transplanting it to another. But, for a moment, try and picture what just one such ingredient could be. What would you pick? For centuries, in medieval Europe, alchemists quested for the “Philosopher’s Stone” that would finally help them achieve their dreams of transmutation. It was a search doomed to failure from the very beginning. And yet, a far better idea was under their noses – or, rather, their underpants – the entire time. My pick? Urine has a strong case for being the most transformative substance in human history. Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter The development of civilisation was built on chemistry. It required the first chemical reaction we mastered – fire – to keep us warm, cook our food and smelt ores. But leatherwork played an equally key role. Urine is a source of urea, which bacteria can break down into ammonia, granting early humans easy access to a base that could soften organic matter and tan hides. Across the world, leatherwork became the cornerstone of survival for every civilisation, from the Americas to Europe, Africa and Asia: even cultures that didn’t develop a bronze age, such as the Aztec, or skipped it entirely, as seen in Sub-Saharan Africa, relied on leatherwork for clothes, structures, industry and commerce. Advertisement If the power of pee helped build civilisation, it would go on to be foundational in its upkeep. In ancient Rome, urine was so useful for laundries to keep togas whiter-than-white that Emperor Vespasian levied a tax on draining urinals. When his son complained, Vespasian’s response was blunt: pecunia non olet , money doesn’t stink. Part of the funds were used to build the Colosseum in Rome, today recognised as one of the wonders of the world. The magic of urine filtered into what would become chemical science, too. Cheimeia , the artisanal trade secrets and recipes found in Alexandria, Egypt, that would later give rise to alchemy, recognised the value of urine. In the Leiden Papyrus X , part of a cluster of the only original manuscripts on alchemy’s origins we still have, you can find a recipe for faking gold using polysulfides. item.title: Read an extract from The Age of Alchemy by Kit Chapman
item.description: The New Scientist Book Club is reading The Age of Alchemy in December “ A handful of lime and another of sulfur in fine powder. Place them in a vessel containing strong vinegar or the urine of a small child. Heat it from below, until the liquid appears like blood. Advertisement Decant this properly, and use. ” Unknown, Leiden Papyrus X , c. 300 CE In 1827, amid the dark, silent balm of an Egyptian night, a graverobber pulled a treasure from the sands. At first, the raider was frustrated; scavenging the tombs near Thebes, he had hoped to uncover a priceless heirloom, or a nugget of gold that would sparkle with lustre in the starlight. Instead, he had found only a clutch of rolled scrolls, made of papyrus and sealed against the elements. For a moment, he considered casting the documents aside and leaving them for the desert. Then greed got the better of him. Westerners loved all things Egyptian, he reasoned. Since the French had arrived with Napoleon, the new field of “Egyptology” had swept the continent, capturing the imagination of scholars and the wealthy. It was almost as popular as the new science of “chemistry”. Surely, if he took his find to the market, he’d find some gullible fool willing to buy it. The buyer’s name was Jean d’Anastasy, and he was anything but a fool. Born in Greece as the son of a Damascus merchant who had won and lost his fortune in the Napoleonic Wars, d’Anastasy had used his family’s connections to set himself up as a grain merchant in Alexandria, before scheming his way into being named the local Consul General for Sweden and Norway. Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter When d’Anastasy wasn’t trading – or rescuing enslaved girls during the Greek War of Independence against the Ottoman Empire – he ran a side-hustle, “procuring” relics from Ancient Egypt and selling them to the salons of Europe: statues to the British Museum in London; rings and jewels to the Louvre in Paris; even a pair of sphinxes that still sit on the banks of the Neva River in St Petersburg. He quickly saw the value of the papers, paid for them, and shipped them back to Europe. Some went to Stockholm, and some to Leiden University in the Netherlands. Among the Leiden trove was one of the most remarkable finds in history: a papyrus scroll with a list of recipes, each with crystal-clear instructions written in Greek. While we have damaged cuneiform tablets and later copies of older works, the Leiden Papyrus X , written around 300 CE, is the oldest surviving alchemy book in history. It is a guide for Egyptian artisans to create wondrous riches, seemingly out of nothing. There are methods on how to polish silverware, cheap alternatives for making knock-off purple robes, and how to create gold lettering by mixing saffron and tortoise bile. These are all real instructions, and all recipes that work (even if, today, there are cheaper ways to get the same result). Among them is the greatest secret in alchemy. It’s called the “invention

item.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
item.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

item.title: People who opposed Tinubu now work with him — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said President Bola Tinubu’s ability to retain former allies and reconcile political opponents demonstrates his capacity to manage Nigeria’s diversity and build consensus. Fashola said politicians who opposed Tinubu in the past had now joined forces with him, describing the president’s ability to bring former adversaries together as evidence of his leadership and capacity to work with others. He spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to why Nigerians should give Tinubu another four years in office. The former minister of works said voters should assess the presidential candidates based on their relationships with people they previously worked with, arguing that the ability to sustain working relationships through difficult periods was an important measure of leadership. “The three main presidential candidates today share one trait in common. They all started as governors. One of them didn’t take office, but he was already a governor-elect, Vice President Atiku Abubakar. Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question for those who want to vote,” Fashola said. He asked why many of those who worked with Tinubu during his time as Lagos governor had remained with him, while political associates of other candidates had moved on. “Where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so out of office when he wasn’t a president. That’s a very good answer to the question,” he said. Fashola said the loyalty of Tinubu’s associates reflected his ability to work with others and manage disagreements without abandoning relationships, adding that such qualities were important for a president leading a country with diverse interests. “It shows an ability to work with others. If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team, and you don’t just get up and jump away when there is crisis in the fold,” he said. He contrasted Tinubu’s political experience with that of other candidates, saying the president remained in the APC despite internal crises, while others left the parties through which they rose to prominence. “There was crisis in the APC. He didn’t leave the party. The others have left the parties that brought them to prominence,” Fashola said. The former governor further argued that Tinubu had expanded his political alliances by bringing former opponents into his fold, including those who once strongly opposed him. “All the people who opposed Tinubu when he used to be called the last man standing. All of them are now working with him. Not just those who worked with him before; those who oppose him are now working with him,” he said. item.title: From fuel subsidy return to Ajaokuta revival; Atiku’s 2027 promises so far
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, tackle insecurity, create jobs and revive key infrastructure projects if elected president in 2027. The African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate has made the pledges at campaign rallies in Sokoto, Bauchi, Yobe and Kogi states, while presenting his proposed policies as measures to reduce the cost of living and improve economic conditions. At the ADC presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on November 4 , Atiku promised to restore petrol subsidy, reopen Nigeria’s land borders to encourage trade and tackle insecurity, including kidnapping, banditry and terrorism. He also pledged to reduce the cost of pilgrimage for Muslim and Christian faithful. Atiku said restoring petrol subsidy would help reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices of essential goods. He also argued that reopening the land borders would benefit farmers, traders and transport operators by stimulating cross-border commerce. At a rally in Bauchi State on November 14, Atiku extended his subsidy promise to electricity, saying he would restore both petroleum and electricity subsidies if elected. He also pledged to strengthen security, particularly in the North-East, resume oil exploration in the Kolmani field and continue the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project. “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue,” he said at the Bauchi rally. At a campaign rally in Yobe State on November 15, Atiku again promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, while pledging to address insecurity and create employment opportunities for young Nigerians. “Let me assure you that once I am elected president in 2027, I will bring back the fuel subsidy,” he said, adding that he would also restore electricity subsidy. He further promised that his administration would work to ensure peace returned to Yobe and other parts of the country, and that young Nigerians would have access to employment opportunities. In Kogi State on November 24 , Atiku campaigned on an “Affordable Life” message, promising to reduce fuel costs, support local production and improve Nigerians’ purchasing power. He said his proposals were aimed at easing the pressure on households, workers and small businesses. At the rally in Lokoja, he also pledged to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill through foreign investment, without relying on government funding for the project. He promised to continue the Baro Port project by dredging the River Niger to enable the port to serve other states and create employment opportunities. “I want to promise you here today that I will revive and complete the Ajaokuta steel mill. This is very doable because we can bring in foreign investment to complete that without

item.title: Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Singer-songwriter and record producer Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has said the “rig and die” slogan sounds correct as a response to election rigging, but warned that innocent people must not be caught up in the resulting violence. He spoke in an interview on Nigeria Info’s WhatsUpLagos show while responding to the slogan ahead of the 2027 elections. The ace singer said frustration over impunity had made calls for severe punishment understandable, while stressing that allegations of rigging must be proven. “You know when a situation gets to a certain point, like right now we’re like on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make you make some kind of statements. This statement sounds correct. It should be like that, actually.” He said the slogan reflected a demand for stronger consequences for election rigging. “If you rig, the punishments should be very severe to deter people from rigging.” 2Baba added: “So the statement itself is rig or die. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzle money and die. Na death penalty for China for embezzlement.” He said Nigeria needed serious deterrence for crimes, including kidnapping, and that people were frustrated by what he described as a lack of consequences. “We’re in a stage where we need, we need serious deterrence, anybody who kidnaps is supposed to face serious consequences. “Because it’s getting too much, and people are just getting away with everything. You understand what I’m saying? So for me, the statement itself, it shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone by. So for me, I don’t see nothing wrong with that statement.” However, he warned against innocent people being harmed in the name of enforcing the slogan. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this fight because some people might not rig, they might just be there. It could be jungle justice without proving that the person actually rigged.” He said the burden of proof should rest on the accusers, while reiterating his support for the statement. “So that’s where, that’s where it becomes dangerous. So the burden of proof should be on the accused person, but the statement in itself, I am in full support of it.” The post Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nvidia: Women Raise Concerns Over Jensen Huang’s Return
item.description: News of Jensen Huang’s shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face. The image was based on a real photo taken in 2024 when Trump survived an assassination attempt during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, and implied that Huang, too, had survived a bid to take him out. For many women, though, the image spoke insultingly to longstanding frustrations about sexism, double standards and a lack of accountability for men in power — across politics and business. Meanwhile, many “tech bros” rushed to Huang’s defense over the past couple of weeks. Billionaire Elon Musk was among many people who signed a petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP Venture capitalist Jason Calacanis described Huang as a “hero” and downplayed the scandal that led to Huang’s resignation as less important than the United States winning the AI race against China. “They’re standing up for the idea that certain men can do whatever they want,” Cleo Capital Managing Director Sarah Kunst told AFP. Part of the problem might be “hero worship,” she said. It also reflects the tech industry’s mythology around “founder mode” — the belief that companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than cede control to executives. Huang resigned on November 12 from Nvidia, the company he cofounded and has led for more than three decades, amid allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman that US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, triggering national security concerns. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Another of Huanga’s alleged lovers was a subordinate at Nvidia. “This is a great example of why integrity matters,” Kunst said. “As soon as I heard about the honeypot element, it was clear to me that there were lapses in judgment that were really big.” On November 17, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Then President Donald Trump intervened. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC, referring to Huang’s reinstatement. Trump himself was found liable in 2023 for sexual assault and defamation and ordered to pay millions as punishment. Dreaded “glass cliff” A trader works on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City on November 2

item.title: Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids
item.description: Volvo provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and accommodation so Ars could drive the XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015 , both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric . As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market . At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-new replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets. So instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base. Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also new, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before. Read full article Comments

item.title: I belong to APC but will protect all parties — Defence Minister
item.description: The Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, has said his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) does not prevent him from carrying out his responsibility to provide security for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. Musa, a retired general, said he was entitled to associate with the ruling party because he was no longer serving in the military. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Arise Television, where he was asked to explain his participation in APC political activities and how he intended to separate his party affiliation from his official duties. “Well, I’m not a military man. I belong to APC, I’m allowed to do that,” he said. The former Chief of Defence Staff maintained that his appearances at political events were also an opportunity to assess security arrangements and ensure that security agencies were performing their duties. He stressed, however, that the responsibility applied to all political parties. “I always want to make sure that whatever is happening anywhere, I go there to ensure that the security forces are doing what they should, and we can do that for everybody. It’s not just for APC. “We are free-minded, we are fair-minded to everybody. We want Nigeria to be safe. We’ll never be a party to any violence,” he said. The minister said President Bola Tinubu had repeatedly cautioned members of his administration against electoral violence. “I know the President has told us on several occasions when we meet, ‘I do not want a violent election. It is not worth it,’” he added. Musa also pledged that the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces would collaborate with political parties and other stakeholders to ensure credible elections in 2027. “Nigerians must understand that we must make our elections free and fair and credible. So we, members of the Armed Forces and the Defence, will ensure that we work together with everyone to make the elections free. “We want every Nigerian to be free to come out and vote for whoever he wants,” he said. On complaints by opposition parties about political violence, Musa argued that disagreements within political parties could also trigger clashes. “Within all the parties, yes! We have found sometimes you see them because somebody feels somebody shouldn’t be there or his name was replaced for whatever reason, then he wants to sabotage from within. So the enemy is not only outside, it’s also within. “Whether the opposition or the party in government, violence is a no-no. And Defence is standing on its feet to ensure that the coming election is free and fair. Whatever it takes for us to do that, we will do that,” he said. The minister urged Nigerians to reject attempts by politicians to recruit them for violent activities, warning that those who lost their lives in political clashes could not be brought back. “We believe that if people are sensitised quite well and they see the folly of going into what they are doing, I mean, look at the few ones that h

item.title: Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he had seen sufficient information that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a security threat, while touting his administration’s intervention to save the scandal-plagued CEO’s job as “a great thing” for the world. “I think he’s absolutely fine,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate. Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation into Huang, Trump said his belief was based on “information I have, which is a lot of information.” Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, was forced to resign earlier this month after revelations that he had an affair with a business executive who reportedly has ties to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export controls. His sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound. Trump revealed that he and other officials in his administration have worked behind the scenes to push for Huang to be reinstated, in a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company’s decision making. “I just thought, I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it’s a great thing that he’s going back,” Trump said Thursday. “So I really… think I did a great thing for our country and even for the world,” Trump said of the effort to back Huang. Asked if he had spoken with Huang since his reinstatement was announced, Trump said no, but then later said: “When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term.” He also praised Huang’s wife as “phenomenal.” The post Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Support team put in an emergency order for vodka – lots of vodka – to bring PCs back online
item.description: The end of the working week is often enough to drive tech support people to drink, which is why The Register likes to get the party started early. Friday mornings bring a new installment of On Call – the column in which we share your stories of doing whatever it takes to keep tech running. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Bruce," who told us that in the mid-2000s he worked for a global radio station. "We used to have about 30 PCs, all running slightly different radio shows depending on the time zone where we broadcast," he explained. The PCs were old clunkers running Windows 95 long after Microsoft ended support for the OS. Management knew the machines needed replacing, but funding was probably another year away. "We had to coax them on till then," Bruce wrote. "And by coax, I mean we were buying RAM on eBay because nobody sold the 4MB sticks we needed anymore." Thanks to the tender ministrations of Bruce and his colleagues, the PCs kept humming and the radio stations stayed on the air. Until a lovely spring Tuesday, when Bruce and his crew enjoyed a bucolic cup of tea in the first real sunshine of the season and received a call informing them that one of the stations was down. One of Bruce's mates figured a cranky old PC probably just needed a reboot and headed off to fix it while the rest of the team enjoyed their tea. And then the phone rang again to report another outage, so Bruce and the entire crew went back to work, chatting about which switch or other shared device could have taken out two PCs. When they arrived in the office, the chap who had gone to reboot the first PC ran in and announced that the computer room had flooded. Bruce and his teammates ran into that room and found dirty brown water all over the floor, walls, ceiling, and the racks holding the ancient PCs. "Water was even spraying out of the front fans of the last two PCs that were still working," Bruce told The Register . "After a lot of shouting words unfit to print, we all got to work ripping them out, shutting down what we could that looked to be working, and started lining them up outside in the car park," Bruce wrote. "Some of us then got to work stripping them down into component parts, others washed them down with isopropanol." As the isopropanol supply dwindled, one of the team arranged an urgent delivery of vodka. "Luckily, it was a gloriously sunny day, so we quickly rinsed the PCs and left them to dry, strewn all over the car park," Bruce wrote. By this stage, he and the team were all filthy and exhausted. With the stations still offline, they had to rebuild the PCs and get them running again. "We only lost two sticks of RAM, one sound card, and a power supply," Bruce wrote. The culprit turned out to be a new hire on the facilities team who, while touring the building, had turned a random tap to see what would happen. item.title: 2027 Elections: INEC raises alarm, warns violence may hurt polls
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri and Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, yesterday, warned that the raging waves of political violence could harm the 2027 general elections. Listing Lagos, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Ebonyi, Delta, Cross River, Oyo and Benue as states where incidents of political violence had been recorded, he warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation and the use of thugs, saying such activities could discourage voter participation and undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections. He also cautioned political parties against signing peace accords in Abuja while allegedly sponsoring violence in states, insisting that no political ambition was worth the blood of Nigerians. According to him, attacks have targeted campaign convoys, town hall meetings, party offices and supporters, while INEC officials, staff and ad hoc personnel have also suffered harassment, intimidation and physical attacks by supporters and agents of political parties, both within Nigeria and abroad. It also said it was working with closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. The warning came as INEC and security agencies met in Abuja to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 polls. This came as the Federal Government assured voters, politicians, electoral officials and political parties of protection before, during and after the elections. Speaking at a Strategic Election Security Conference jointly convened by INEC and the Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA, Amupitan said Nigeria had witnessed a disturbing escalation in political intolerance, inflammatory rhetoric and coordinated attacks since the commencement of campaigns in August 2026. Addressing political parties, he said: “Signing peace accords in Abuja while tolerating or financing thuggery in the states is a contradiction our democracy can no longer afford.” He warned that INEC would not succumb to threats or intimidation. “We will neither be intimidated nor blackmailed into compromising our neutrality, and every attack on INEC personnel, facilities, or materials will be met with the full weight of the law,” INEC chairman said. Amupitan said responsibility for electoral violence extended beyond those directly involved in attacks, stressing that political party leaders must be held accountable for the conduct of their candidates and supporters. He said: “Accountability does not end with the foot soldiers who throw stones or wield weapons,” adding that “party leadership bears moral and political responsibility for the conduct of its candidates, campaign councils, and youth wings”. Violence may suppress voter turnout The INEC chairman identified three major consequences of political violence for the electoral process, including voter suppression, threats to the safety of electoral personnel and the possibility of post-election violence. item.title: 2027: 2Baba backs ‘rig and die’ slogan, demands severe penalties
item.description: Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has backed the controversial “rig and die” slogan associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying anyone caught manipulating election results in 2027 should face severe punishment. The singer, however, cautioned against innocent people being victimised in the process, insisting that elections should not be treated as warfare. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Nigeria Info 99.3, where he described Nigeria’s political atmosphere as tense and said the slogan reflected growing public frustration over the country’s situation. “You know, when the situation gets to a certain point, like right now, we’re on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make people make some kinds of statements. “The statement sounds correct, right? It sounds correct. It should be like that, actually. For the circumstances. Like, if you rig, the punishments will be very severe to deter people from rigging,” 2Baba said. The singer said he saw nothing wrong with the slogan, arguing that stringent penalties would discourage electoral malpractice. “The statement itself is ‘rig and die’. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzlement and die. Now, there’s that penalty for embezzlement in China,” he said. 2Baba also called for severe consequences for kidnappers, particularly those targeting schools, arguing that the absence of adequate deterrence had allowed criminal activities to persist. “We’re in a state where we need serious deterrence for anybody who kidnaps in our schools to face serious consequences, so that others will not do it. Because it’s getting too much and people are just getting away with everything,” he said. The ‘African Queen’ crooner said the slogan reflected the level of frustration among Nigerians but warned against punishing people without evidence of wrongdoing. “For me, the statement itself shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone bad. So, for me, I don’t see anything wrong with that statement. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this,” he added. During the interview, the presenter recalled 2Baba’s longstanding advocacy for peaceful electoral participation, including his message urging Nigerians to vote rather than fight during elections. Asked about Nigerians who might sell their votes because of economic hardship, the singer described the situation as unfortunate, noting that people facing difficult conditions could easily become vulnerable to manipulation. He also called for proper reorientation, urging Nigerians to address internal challenges rather than allow external interests to influence the country. The “rig and die” slogan has featured prominently in political discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly among supporters of the NDC and its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. item.title: AWS adds virtual iPhones to its cloud
item.description: AWS now offers two new types of cloudy computers: emulated Androids and simulated iPhones. The cloudy colossus announced both virtual offerings on Wednesday. They’re part of its Device Farm service, which previously saw AWS offer developers the chance to test their software on actual iOS and Android devices that reside in the Amazonian cloud. AWS will now also host virtual devices running Android and iOS. AWS touts the virtual mobile devices as superior to physical devices. “With virtual devices, you can shift testing left to stages that need high speed and volume, such as pull requests, code merges, and smoke tests, and keep real devices for later stages that need high fidelity, such as regression and release testing,” the cloudy business unit argues in its launch announcement. AWS also says developers can get to work faster on a virtual iPhone or Pixel. “Virtual devices running the latest device and OS typically start in seconds, and others start in around a minute,” the outfit argues. That may sound appetizing, but Amazon’s menu of virtual devices is short and bland. When The Register logged on as an AWS user, the only emulated Android phone listed was a Google Pixel 10, running Android 15, 16, or 17. An emulated Pixel tablet running Android 17 is also on the menu. At the time of writing, we could find only a virtual iPhone 16, running iOS 18.6, 23.61, and 27.0. Analyst firm Counterpoint’s list of the world’s top 10 best-selling smartphones in Q2 of 2026 does not include a single Pixel device. The iPhone 16 occupies 10 th place. iPhone 17 models occupy the first, second, third, and seventh place on the list. AWS might excite more developers if it adds emulators for the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Galaxy A07 4G, A17 5G, A17 4G, and Galaxy S26, as they occupy the fourth, fifth, sixth, eighth and ninth places on Counterpoint’s list. Amazon’s choice of a Pixel tablet is also an oddity given analyst firm IDC doesn’t list Google among its top five tablet vendors . Amazon does offer physical Galaxy A17 devices and three versions of the iPhone 17. But Device Farm doesn’t offer any foldable devices, meaning developers struggling to wrap their heads around the iPhone Duo will need either ask Apple for a loaner or shell out $2,000 to acquire one. At least developers don’t have to change behavior to access the few virtual devices AWS offers, as existing Device Farm APIs and test frameworks will work on real or notional machines. ®

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 27 – The Moon Watchers
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 27 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The Moon Watchers Explanation: On November 24 , all denizens of our fair planet could watch the Moon rise opposite the setting Sun. Easy to spot in twilight skies above fields, fences, backyards, and even stone walls, the Moon was big and bright, and at its full phase . Known to some as a Beaver Moon, November’s Full Moon was also near perigee, the closest point in its elliptical orbit around planet Earth. That made it one of the biggest and brightest Full Moons, also known as a supermoon . In fact, November’s Full Moon was the first in a series of four consecutive Full Moon’s near perigee. So your next chance to watch a supermoon rise will be when the Cold Moon rises on December 23. item.title: Shivelyuch Socked In
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Shivelyuch Socked In Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the same way that Shivelyuch (also called Shiveluch) frequently displays volcanic activity, it is also chronically obscured by clouds. When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on November 8, 2026, clouds encroached on the snowy mountain on Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula . But they hovered beneath the volcano’s 3,283-meter (10,771-foot) peak, leaving a clear opening over its caldera and northern upper slopes. The upper reaches of Shivelyuch feature a caldera 9 kilometers (5.6 miles) wide that is open to the south. A lava dome , formed by vents extruding viscous magma, appears as a dark area within it. Lava domes on Shivelyuch go through cycles of growth and collapse, with collapses sometimes setting off fast-moving avalanches of hot ash and rock called pyroclastic flows . In November 2026, effusive eruptions of lava and explosive activity at Shivelyuch had been ongoing for months , according to reports from the Kamchatka Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT). And despite frequent cloudiness, satellites regularly detect thermal anomalies from the volcano. On the day of this image, KVERT reported that a plume of resuspended ash drifted 120 kilometers (75 miles) to the east. That kind of activity is relatively tame for the mountain. Explosions from Shivelyuch periodically send ash several kilometers up into the atmosphere, where it can travel great distances and pose risks to aircraft . In July 2026, an ash plume rode the jet stream over the Bering Sea into Alaskan airspace, according to news reports , prompting the cancellation of multiple flights. NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey . Story by Lindsey Doermann. item.title: Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug
item.description: India’s free e-government platform has a critical SQL injection flaw that thousands of organizations must patch to protect up to two billion citizens. The platform is called the Digital Infrastructure for Governance (Impact and Transformation) – aka DIGIT – and is a modular suite that offers common services such as authentication and payment collection. Third party developers can also create DIGIT modules, and plenty have done so and now offer add-ons that handle tasks as diverse as managing birth and death certificates, revenue collection, and running water treatment plants. DIGIT is ubiquitous in India, where all state and union territory governments use the platform, as do over 20,000 local government entities. India also exports DIGIT under its policy of turning software created for its own needs into “digital public goods” (DPI) that it happily gives away to other nations. Nine nations have implemented DIGIT to some degree, among them Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Nigeria, Burundi, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Jamaica, and Sri Lanka India’s population is 1.4 billion. Indonesia’s is 280 million and Nigeria is home to 240 million. DIGIT is therefore used by governments that serve over two billion people, some of whom are now at risk thanks to CVE-2026-136706 , a 9.3-rated SQL injection flaw present in DIGIT which allows “improper neutralization of user supplied input while constructing SQL queries and execution in the affected User and Access Control Service components.” “An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted input through the affected API endpoint to the targeted system,” according to CERT-IN . “Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries, potentially resulting in unauthorized disclosure, modification or deletion of database information on the targeted system.” eGov India, which oversees work on DIGIT, has released source code for an update that fixes the problem. While local government users of DIGIT typically access it as SaaS, through large implementations run by national or state governments, over 1,000 deployments are live across various cities and other entities. Those orgs can therefore add patching DIGIT to their urgent to-do lists, along with fixing Java , PHP , vCenter and any other widely used technologies that suddenly need an urgent security update. ®

item.title: The token factory never sleeps
item.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30
